findings.element: Matching rules modal (link in How we get the data)
findings.finding: The modal says Date is a match key and requires "same calendar day", but the sourced spec says matching is a 3-pass ID cascade on ID + amount and never compares dates.
findings.user_impact: An accountant who trusts this modal will expect settlement-lag items (for example a charge on Aug 31 and a QuickBooks entry on Sep 1) to come back unmatched, and may post manual adjusting entries or split the period to work around a rule that doesn't exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the modal match the engine: list the ID-cascade passes on ID + amount and say outright that dates are not compared; if "Fuzzy amount ±0.01" isn't in the spec, remove it or get a source for it.

evidence.source: context.md Domain facts (SET spec Confluence 3701506049): "Matching is a 3-pass ID cascade on ID + amount. Dates are never compared when matching."

findings.finding: A custom range that ends today was accepted and the run started, even though the spec says today's date can't be selected; the inputs also have no min or max.
findings.user_impact: Running on a day that isn't finished captures a partial set of integration and QuickBooks transactions, so items still in flight show up as false unmatched differences, and that period then blocks any later non-overlapping rerun on the same clearing account.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the end-date max to yesterday (today minus 1) and refuse ranges that include today or later, using an inline message that names the rule.

evidence.source: context.md Domain facts: "Today's date cannot be selected." (SET spec Confluence 3701506049); statemap controls[] Custom start/end date inputs: started=true, input min="" max=""

findings.element: Account to reconcile > Shopify optgroup, and Integration Import method for Shopify
findings.finding: For Shopify the prototype offers only Assisted and Manual and puts "Shopify clearing (Synder)" in the manual-upload group, but the spec gives Shopify Automated and Manual only: no Assisted, and the clearing account should be in the automated group.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper reconciling the Shopify clearing account is made to export and upload payout files by hand for a source that the spec says can be imported automatically. The Assisted payouts-only path also isn't a spec mode, so what gets compared may differ from production.
findings.suggested_fix: Get Ignat's decision on the spec-vs-prototype question, then either give Shopify Automated/Manual with its clearing accounts in the automated group, or record why the spec doesn't apply.

evidence.source: context.md Domain facts, Modes per spec: "Shopify: Automated / Manual. The prototype shows Assisted/Manual"; statemap observations: Shopify accounts all under "Synder accounts (manual file upload required)"

gaps: Overlapping periods: no run was tried on the same clearing account with a period that overlaps an existing reconciliation, so the spec rule that same-account periods can't overlap is unverified.

Retrieval failure states are in not_exercised: nobody checked whether a failed automatic retrieval names the failed precondition (lost QBO authorization, closed period, multi-currency off, missing mapping), as KF-9 asks.

Vocabulary deviations below the 3-finding cap: the date tooltip says "on the platform" (vocabulary.md: Integration, not platform), and the automatic card says "Synder pulls QuickBooks and Stripe" (vocabulary.md: Import, not fetch/pull).
